title: Messi's Magic Runs Out, But Argentina Finds a New Hero!
summary: Have you ever watched a soccer game where your team almost loses, but then someone saves the day at the very last second? That's exactly what happened to Argentina on Saturday night in Kansas City! The defending World Cup champions were stuck in a 1-1 tie against Switzerland, and the clock was ticking. If nobody scored soon, the game would go to penalty kicks—which are super stressful, like a game of chance. But then, in the 112th minute, Julián Alvarez did something amazing. He kicked a right-footed rocket that zoomed into the far upper corner of the goal! The crowd of 69,045 fans went wild. Later, Lautaro Martínez added another goal, and Argentina won 3-1. Now they're going to the semifinals to play England on Wednesday in Atlanta. You might be wondering: where was Lionel Messi, the most famous soccer player in the world? He helped with an early assist, but he didn't score a goal himself. That's a big deal because Messi had scored in nine straight World Cup games—a record! This was his first game in 10 matches without a goal. Switzerland played really tough, even after one of their players got a red card and had to leave the field. Their forward Dan Ndoye tied the game in the second half by slipping the ball under Argentina's goalie. But Argentina didn't give up. Now they're two wins away from another World Cup trophy. Can they do it?
why_it_matters: This game shows that even your heroes need help sometimes, and teamwork can lead to victory—just like when a classmate steps up to help in a group project.

background_read: The FIFA World Cup is the most important soccer tournament, taking place every four years. Argentina won the trophy in 2022, with their star player Lionel Messi (widely considered one of the best ever). The match was played in Kansas City, a big city in the United States.
Article_Structure: WHO: Argentina's soccer team (Julián Alvarez, Lautaro Martínez, Lionel Messi) and Switzerland (Dan Ndoye).
WHAT: Argentina beat Switzerland 3-1 in a World Cup quarterfinal; Julián Alvarez scored a late winning goal in extra time.
WHY: Argentina needed a win to reach the semifinals, and even without a Messi goal, other players stepped up to secure the victory.

perspectives.description: They are thrilled because the team fought back and found a new hero, showing they can win even when Messi doesn't score.
Some fans fear that Messi's goalless streak could be a problem in the next round if the team relies too much on him.
They point out that true champion teams have many players who can win matches, and Argentina proved that depth today.
